findings.title: Settled knowledge before compelled sight
findings.claim: At the focus's knowing words, settled knowledge is presented as a condition whose unrealized effect would interrupt competitive diversion and alter conduct before later compelled seeing.

Their contact makes a behavioral consequence of the omitted conditional legible before later disclosure.
findings.reader_payoff: Certainty becomes perceptible as knowledge with an expected effect in attention and conduct, rather than as private mental assent alone.
findings.containment: The focus still says, in its primary floor, that they would know with certainty. The interruption of diversion is an inferred consequence of the conditional, not an omitted quotation. The legacy reader-walk citations for ل ه و and ك ث ر have no registered branches and are not promoted to lexical findings.

epistemic.reason: The focus carriers and published support are directly supplied, while the behavioral consequence and its timing are inferred from wider connection nominations; duplicate legacy walks remain explicitly qualified.
